title: Newton's Laws Adventure
welcome_lead: Meet Sir Isaac's three laws of motion — the rules every moving thing obeys. 🍎
meta_desc: Newton's Laws Adventure — GCSE Physics: the first, second, and third laws explained with everyday examples.
final_note: You learned the three laws: inertia, F = ma, and action-reaction pairs. The basics every physicist knows.

walkthroughs.body_html:
An object stays still, or moves at constant velocity, unless a resultant force acts on it.

That's why your bag slides forward when the bus stops suddenly — its inertia wants it to keep moving.

Heavier objects have more inertia. They're harder to start or stop.

A resultant force makes a mass accelerate: F = m × a.

Same force on a lighter object = bigger acceleration. Same mass with bigger force = bigger acceleration.

Units: F in newtons, m in kilograms, a in m/s².

Every action has an equal and opposite reaction.

Push a wall with 50 N — the wall pushes you back with 50 N. That's how you walk, swim, and how rockets fly. 🚀

The two forces act on different objects, which is why they don't cancel out.

mcqs.q: Newton's 1st law is also known as:
options: The law of gravity
The law of inertia
The law of action-reaction
The law of acceleration

mcqs.q: If the resultant force on an object is zero, the object:
options: Always stops
Speeds up
Keeps constant velocity
Slows down

mcqs.q: If an object is moving at constant velocity in a straight line, what is the net force on it?
options: The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
There must be a forward force on the object to keep it moving.
Zero — by Newton's first law, constant velocity requires zero net force.
Negative acceleration means the car is moving backwards.

mcqs.q: When you push a wall, what does Newton's third law say about the wall?
options: The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.
The wall exerts an equal and opposite force on you at the same instant.
The wall only pushes back if your force is strong enough to make it react.
Negative acceleration means the car is moving backwards.

mcqs.q: If a car has negative acceleration, what does that necessarily mean?
options: Its acceleration is in the negative direction (often opposite to the chosen positive direction); it may be slowing down or speeding up in reverse.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
Negative acceleration means the car is moving backwards.
Negative acceleration always means the car is slowing down.
